tasks.prompt: Hot water jetting clears a grease sewer quickly, but the downstream lift station then fouls its floats the same day.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario grease sewer upstream of a lift station. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: The sewer clears during hot jetting and large grease chunks are seen passing the downstream manhole.
No grease collection or vacuum was used at the downstream manhole during jetting.
That evening the lift station floats foul and the station alarms on high level.
Grease chunks matching the sewer returns are found coating the station floats.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Jetting moved the grease downstream without collection, and it fouled the station floats
The lift station generates its own grease independent of the sewer
The station floats failed electrically on the same day by chance
Hot water damaged the sewer so it released pipe material to the station

inference.explanation: Grease was seen passing downstream uncollected, and matching chunks fouled the floats the same evening. That is transfer of the same material, not an independent station source or an electrical fault.

nextClue.prompt: Which practice check best confirms the transfer for the work plan change?

options.label: Sewer pipe material records
Downstream manhole log during jetting showing chunks passing with no vacuum collection in place
Station electrical test records

nextClue.explanation: The manhole log documents the missing collection step that let grease travel to the station.

clueText.nc-a: Pipe material records do not explain grease chunks arriving at the floats.
clueText.nc-b: The log shows chunks passing the manhole for an hour with no vacuum truck stationed there.
clueText.nc-c: Floats fouled with matching grease chunks point to material fouling, not an electrical fault.

tasks.prompt: A sewer blocks repeatedly below a construction site and returns contain sand, gravel, and pieces of concrete.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario sewer below an active construction site. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Returns from jetting are sand, gravel, and angular concrete pieces.
CCTV shows a pile of granular debris on the invert below a site lateral.
The same reach ran clear for years before construction started.
Upstream of the site lateral the pipe is clean on CCTV.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Tree roots are crushing the pipe and releasing concrete pieces
The pipe bedding is entering through a broken wall
Residents are flushing renovation waste from homes
Construction debris is entering through the site connection and settling in the main

inference.explanation: Clean pipe upstream, debris piled below the site lateral, angular construction material, and a clear history before construction all point to the site. Bedding entry would show a wall defect, which is not reported.

nextClue.prompt: Which check best confirms the entry point for site follow up?

options.label: Inspection of the site connection and its sediment control during a site washdown
Root defect log for the reach
A survey of home renovations on the street

nextClue.explanation: Watching the connection during washdown tests whether site water carries debris into the main.

clueText.nc-a: Washdown water at the connection runs sandy and debris appears at the downstream manhole minutes later.
clueText.nc-b: No root defects were reported on this reach camera run.
clueText.nc-c: The debris is angular site material piled below the site lateral, not home waste.

tasks.prompt: After a watermain break on the same street, the sewer surcharges with sandy water even in dry weather.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario street after a watermain break. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Sewer flow stays high for two days after the watermain is repaired and the street is dry.
Manhole inspection shows clear water jetting in at a sewer joint near the break location.
The incoming water tests low in chlorine residual, unlike treated watermain water at the tap, but is clear and sandy.
When the watermain zone is briefly isolated for a test, the sewer inflow slows noticeably.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Groundwater alone explains a two day surge after the break
A home sump pump started discharging the same day
Watermain water is reaching the sewer through damaged ground and the open sewer joint near the break
Rainfall inflow is surcharging the sewer

inference.explanation: Clear water jetting at a joint beside the break, and inflow slowing when the watermain zone is isolated, tie the surge to the watermain event. It is dry, ruling out rainfall, and groundwater alone would not respond to the isolation test.

nextClue.prompt: Which test best confirms the link before the sewer joint is repaired?

options.label: Rain gauge review for the week
Sump pump survey of nearby homes
Repeat zone isolation with a flow log at the downstream manhole showing inflow falling and recovering

nextClue.explanation: A repeat isolation with a flow log gives a controlled on and off test of the watermain link.

clueText.nc-a: The street was dry, so rain records cannot explain the surge.
clueText.nc-b: A sump survey cannot explain inflow that responds to watermain isolation.
clueText.nc-c: The log shows inflow dropping during isolation and returning when the zone is restored, twice in a row.

tasks.prompt: A sewer reach loses flow capacity over years and CCTV shows the pipe is oval, with the crown pushed down.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario older sewer with shape change. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: CCTV shows the flexible pipe deflected into an oval, crown down by about 15 percent of diameter.
The pipe barrel has no cracks and joints are tight with no roots.
Heavy truck traffic uses the road above and the cover over the pipe is shallow.
Flow capacity complaints match peak hours when the deflected section runs full.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The camera lens distorted a round pipe into an oval
The flexible pipe has deflected under load and lost capacity, without a joint or root failure
Roots have crushed the pipe into an oval
Grease has built up evenly to shrink the pipe into an oval

inference.explanation: Tight joints with no roots, an uncracked barrel, shallow cover under truck traffic, and a measured crown drop fit load deflection of flexible pipe. A lens fault would affect other reaches on the same run, which is not reported.

nextClue.prompt: Which measurement best confirms deflection for the repair decision?

options.label: A grease thickness sample from the crown
Laser profile or mandrel measurement of the deflected section compared with the nominal diameter
A root cutting trial in the section

nextClue.explanation: A profile measurement quantifies the shape loss that the repair decision depends on.

clueText.nc-a: No grease coating was reported on this camera run.
clueText.nc-b: The profile shows 15 percent vertical deflection at mid reach and near round pipe at both manholes.
clueText.nc-c: No roots were seen, so a cutting trial has nothing to test.

tasks.prompt: Backups occur at one low home only, and only when a nearby combined sewer surcharges in heavy rain.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario low home near a combined sewer. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: The home is the lowest on the street and its basement fixtures sit below the manhole rim level.
Backups match heavy rain events and street manhole surcharge records.
Neighbours with higher basements on the same street stay dry in the same storms.
A backwater valve on the home lateral is found open and fouled with debris when checked.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Storm surcharge in the street sewer backs into the low home through its unprotected lateral
The home lateral is blocked by roots at all times
The home plumbing is undersized for its own fixtures
Groundwater floods the basement through the floor in every rain

inference.explanation: Rain matched backups, a surcharging street sewer, higher neighbours staying dry, and a fouled open backwater valve fit surcharge entry through the lateral. A constant root blockage would also back up in dry weather from the home own flow.

nextClue.prompt: Which check best confirms the entry route during the next storm watch?

options.label: Basement fixture and lateral cleanout watch during a storm, noting flow direction at the cleanout as the street surcharges
A dry weather lateral camera run
A floor drain dye test in dry weather

nextClue.explanation: Watching flow direction at the cleanout while the street surcharges directly tests the entry route.

clueText.nc-a: The cleanout shows flow moving toward the house as the manhole surcharges, then reversing as levels fall.
clueText.nc-b: A dry weather camera cannot show a storm only surcharge route.
clueText.nc-c: A dry weather dye test cannot reproduce storm surcharge levels.

tasks.prompt: CCTV shows a brick missing from a manhole benching channel and bricks sitting in the sewer outlet.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario brick manhole inspection. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Bricks matching the benching are lodged at the outlet and partly block flow.
The benching has a gap where one brick is missing and mortar is crumbled.
Upstream sewers are clear on CCTV with no brick debris.
After the lodged bricks are removed, flow improves but the benching gap remains.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Bricks were flushed down from homes upstream
The sewer pipe itself is collapsing and dropping bricks
A contractor dumped bricks into the manhole the same week
Bench bricks have fallen into the outlet and are obstructing flow at the manhole

inference.explanation: Matching bricks, a gap in the benching with crumbled mortar, clear upstream sewers, and flow improving on removal all locate the source at the manhole benching. The sewer pipe is not brick in this system.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms the manhole as the source for the repair order?

options.label: Upstream CCTV report
Contractor delivery records for the week
Manhole condition log with photos of the benching gap and the recovered bricks side by side

nextClue.explanation: Photos tying the gap to the recovered bricks document the manhole defect as the source.

clueText.nc-a: Upstream CCTV was already clear, so it cannot be the brick source.
clueText.nc-b: No dumping was reported and the benching gap explains the bricks without it.
clueText.nc-c: The log shows the benching gap shape matches the recovered bricks and the mortar is crumbled around it.

tasks.prompt: A sewer blocks with wipes and rags always at the same bend, and cleaning upstream reaches finds very few wipes.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario sewer with a ragging bend. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Rag balls removed at the bend are made of wipes and fabric strips.
CCTV shows a protruding lateral connection at the bend catching fibres.
Upstream reaches on camera carry few wipes and no rag balls.
After the protruding connection is trimmed flush, ragging at the bend stops for a year.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The bend is too sharp for any flow to pass wipes
Roots at the bend are catching the wipes
Wipes snag on the protruding connection at the bend and build rag balls there
Wipes are discharged only by homes right at the bend

inference.explanation: A protruding connection at the exact snag point, few wipes upstream in transit, and a full year clear after trimming it flush confirm the snag mechanism. No roots were reported at the bend.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best documents the snag mechanism for other similar sites?

options.label: Bend angle measurement from as built drawings
CCTV stills of fibres caught on the protrusion before trimming and the clear bend after trimming
Wipe brand survey of nearby homes

nextClue.explanation: Before and after stills at the same protrusion document cause and fix for reuse at other sites.

clueText.nc-a: The bend angle did not change, yet ragging stopped after trimming, so angle alone was not the cause.
clueText.nc-b: Stills show fibre tails streaming from the protrusion before, and a clean flush joint after trimming.
clueText.nc-c: Wipe brands do not explain why ragging happened at one bend only.

tasks.prompt: Flow through a trunk sewer falls over a dry week and divers find a shopping cart and timber lodged at a creek crossing siphon inlet.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario siphon inlet inspection. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Dry weather flow at the downstream meter falls day by day for a week.
Upstream manhole levels rise over the same week while downstream levels stay normal.
Divers at the siphon inlet clear a shopping cart, timber, and matted debris.
Immediately after clearing, upstream levels fall and metered flow returns to normal.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The flow meter drifted low over the week
Large debris lodged at the siphon inlet was progressively blocking the trunk
A downstream treatment plant restriction was backing up the trunk
Infiltration fell during the dry week and reduced flow

inference.explanation: Rising upstream levels with normal downstream levels locate a restriction between them, and clearing debris at that point restores both. A meter fault would not raise upstream levels or respond to clearing.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms the inlet as the restriction point?

options.label: Paired level log, upstream and downstream of the siphon, before and after the debris clearing
Flow meter calibration certificate
Rainfall log for the dry week

nextClue.explanation: Paired levels isolate the head loss to the siphon reach and show it vanish after clearing.

clueText.nc-a: The log shows a growing level difference across the siphon that returns to normal after clearing.
clueText.nc-b: Calibration does not explain upstream levels rising and then falling on clearing.
clueText.nc-c: The week was dry, so rainfall cannot explain the pattern.

tasks.prompt: A new subdivision sewer blocks within its first year and CCTV shows grout and a displaced gasket in the pipe.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario new subdivision sewer. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: CCTV shows hardened grout fins on the invert at several joints.
One joint shows a displaced gasket partly hanging into the flow.
Debris and wipes are collecting on the grout fins and at the gasket.
Older sewers downstream of the subdivision are clear and problem free.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Construction defects in the new pipe, grout fins and a displaced gasket, are catching debris
Residents of the new homes flush far more wipes than the older area
Roots have invaded the new pipe within its first year
The downstream older sewer is backing debris up into the new pipe

inference.explanation: Grout fins and a displaced gasket are seen catching debris, and the downstream older sewer is clear. New tight joints with construction defects fit the first year timing better than roots, which are not reported.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best supports a warranty repair claim for the new sewer?

options.label: A wipe use survey of the new homes
A root treatment quote for the reach
CCTV defect log with joint numbers, grout locations, and the gasket defect, tied to the as built drawings

nextClue.explanation: A defect log tied to drawings documents construction defects at specific joints for the warranty claim.

clueText.nc-a: A survey cannot explain grout fins and a displaced gasket seen on camera.
clueText.nc-b: No roots were seen in the new pipe on this camera run.
clueText.nc-c: The log lists grout at six joints and the displaced gasket at joint nine, all matching as built joint numbers.

tasks.prompt: A sewer surcharges in dry weather below a school, and the blockage is paper and pencils mixed with grit.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario sewer below a school. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: The blockage material is paper, pencils, and grit matted together.
Backups occur on school days and ease during school holidays.
CCTV shows debris entering from the school lateral during the school day.
Homes upstream and downstream of the school lateral drain normally.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Grit from road sanding is the sole cause of the blockage
Roots from schoolyard trees filled the pipe with paper
The sewer grade failed suddenly below the school
Material discharged from the school lateral is building the blockage below it

inference.explanation: Pencils and paper in the mass, a school day pattern, and debris seen entering from the school lateral locate the source. Road grit alone would not carry pencils or follow the school calendar.

nextClue.prompt: Which check best confirms the school source for the follow up meeting?

options.label: Tree inventory for the schoolyard
Lateral observation during a school day showing debris discharge, logged with times
Road sanding tonnage records

nextClue.explanation: Timed observation of the lateral discharge during school hours directly ties the material to the school.

clueText.nc-a: No roots were reported in the blockage material or on camera.
clueText.nc-b: The log shows paper and pencil debris leaving the lateral at lunch washroom peaks on two school days.
clueText.nc-c: Sanding grit does not include pencils and does not follow school holidays.

tasks.prompt: Jetting returns from a blocked reach include chunks of black pipe wall and the CCTV shows a longitudinal crack.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario blocked reach with pipe fragments. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Returns include rigid black fragments matching the plastic pipe wall.
CCTV shows a longitudinal crack with one edge lifted into the flow.
Debris snags on the lifted crack edge and builds the blockage.
The rest of the reach is round, uncracked, and clear.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The fragments are pieces of a jetting hose left in the pipe
Roots cracked the pipe this week and caused an instant blockage
A cracked pipe section with a lifted edge is snagging debris and causing the blockage
The fragments are hardened grease dyed black

inference.explanation: Rigid wall matching fragments, a visible crack with a lifted snag edge, and debris building at that edge locate a structural snag. Grease is not rigid pipe wall, and no hose loss was reported.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best defines the structural repair for this reach?

options.label: CCTV crack log with length, clock position, and distances from both manholes
A grease sample analysis
A jetting hose inventory

nextClue.explanation: A crack log with length and position defines the lining or replacement limits.

clueText.nc-a: The log shows a 3 m crack at the spring line with the lifted edge, sound pipe beyond both ends.
clueText.nc-b: The fragments are rigid pipe wall, not grease, so analysis adds nothing.
clueText.nc-c: No hose was reported missing and the crack is visible on camera.

tasks.prompt: Dry weather flow in a sewer catchment doubles overnight and stays high for a week with no rain.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario catchment flow study, dry week. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Night flow at the meter rises from 4 L/s to 9 L/s and stays there day and night.
The extra water is clear and cold, and a drinking water reservoir level in the same area is falling faster than use explains.
Isolating sewer sections by temporary plugs shows the extra flow enters in one 200 m reach.
That reach runs beside a watermain that was recently repaired.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Snowmelt is entering through manholes across the catchment
A steady clear water inflow entering in one reach, consistent with a watermain leak reaching the sewer
Rainfall inflow is doubling the catchment flow
A new factory started discharging to the catchment that week

inference.explanation: The week is dry, the rise is steady day and night, and plug isolation locates entry in one reach beside a repaired watermain. A factory discharge would vary with work hours and snowmelt would not isolate to one reach.

nextClue.prompt: Which test best confirms the watermain link in that reach?

options.label: Factory production records for the week
Snow depth records for the catchment
Watermain pressure zone step test with sewer flow logged at the reach manholes

nextClue.explanation: A step test that moves sewer flow when watermain pressure changes confirms the hydraulic link.

clueText.nc-a: No factory change is stated, and the inflow is steady through nights and the weekend.
clueText.nc-b: The entry isolates to one reach, not across catchment manholes as snowmelt would.
clueText.nc-c: Sewer inflow in the reach falls as the zone pressure is stepped down and recovers as it is restored.

tasks.prompt: Sewer flow spikes within an hour of rain starting and falls within an hour of rain ending, every storm.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario catchment with storm response. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Flow rises sharply with each storm and returns to dry weather flow within an hour of rain ending.
Dry weather night flow is low and steady, showing little groundwater entry.
Smoke testing finds several roof leaders and a yard drain connected to the sanitary sewer.
Dye placed in one connected yard drain appears in the sanitary manhole within minutes.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Direct stormwater connections are driving fast inflow during rain
Groundwater infiltration through pipe joints drives the storm spikes
The treatment plant is returning flow to the catchment during rain
Pump stations upstream surge during rain and cause the spikes

inference.explanation: A one hour rise and fall with rain, low dry night flow, and dye proven direct connections fit inflow, not groundwater, which responds slowly and would keep night flow high.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best supports a disconnection program for this catchment?

options.label: Pump station run records during storms
Smoke and dye log listing each confirmed direct connection by address
Groundwater well levels for the catchment

nextClue.explanation: A confirmed connection list by address is the actionable record for disconnections.

clueText.nc-a: Pump records do not explain dye arriving from a yard drain in minutes.
clueText.nc-b: The log lists nine roof leaders and two yard drains dye confirmed to the sanitary sewer.
clueText.nc-c: Well levels change slowly and cannot explain one hour storm spikes.

tasks.prompt: Night flow in an old catchment stays high all year, rises slowly after long wet periods, and barely reacts to single storms.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario old catchment, year of flow data. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Minimum night flow is 60 percent of average day flow, far above the water use pattern for the area.
Night flow climbs over weeks of wet weather and falls over weeks of dry weather.
Single storms add only a small brief bump to flow.
CCTV shows many joints with mineral deposits and fine roots, and groundwater is high in local wells.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Roof leaders connected to the sewer dominate the extra flow
A watermain leak in one reach dominates the extra flow
Illegal storm connections dominate the extra flow
Groundwater infiltration through many defective joints is the dominant extra flow

inference.explanation: Slow seasonal response, persistently high night flow, and widespread joint defects with high groundwater fit infiltration. Direct connections would spike with single storms, and a single leak would not track seasonal groundwater.

nextClue.prompt: Which analysis best confirms infiltration dominance for rehabilitation planning?

options.label: Night flow trend plotted against groundwater levels and rainfall over the full year
A single storm flow hydrograph
A one day watermain pressure log

nextClue.explanation: A year long trend against groundwater shows the slow seasonal tracking that defines infiltration.

clueText.nc-a: Night flow tracks groundwater with a lag of days and ignores single storms, across all four seasons.
clueText.nc-b: One storm hydrograph only captures the small brief bump, not the year round base.
clueText.nc-c: One day of pressure cannot explain a seasonal pattern across the whole catchment.

tasks.prompt: One manhole surcharges in moderate rain while manholes upstream and downstream of it do not.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario manhole surcharge investigation. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Only the middle manhole of three surcharges in moderate rain.
Inspection shows its cover has open pick holes and sits in a paved low spot that ponds in rain.
The two neighbouring manholes have sealed covers and sit above ponding levels.
Sealing the pick holes for one storm as a trial stops the surcharge at that manhole.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Groundwater enters the manhole walls under pressure
A roof leader connects directly into this manhole barrel
Rain enters through the open cover in the ponding low spot and surcharges that manhole locally
The sewer below the manhole is blocked and backs up only there

inference.explanation: Only the ponding manhole with open holes surcharges, neighbours stay normal, and a sealing trial stops it. A downstream blockage would raise upstream levels too, not just one manhole.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms the cover entry route?

options.label: CCTV of the sewer below the manhole
Groundwater levels in nearby wells
Storm watch log with ponding depth at the cover and surcharge timing before and after sealing

nextClue.explanation: Ponding depth matched to surcharge timing, changing with sealing, proves the cover route.

clueText.nc-a: The sewer below was not reported blocked, and upstream manholes stayed normal.
clueText.nc-b: Well levels do not change with one cover sealing trial.
clueText.nc-c: The log shows surcharge only when ponding covers the holes, and no surcharge after sealing in a similar storm.

tasks.prompt: Flow monitoring shows one subcatchment produces three times the wet weather flow per home of its neighbours.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario subcatchment flow comparison. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Dry weather flows per home are similar across all three subcatchments.
In rain, the suspect subcatchment peaks at three times the per home flow of the others.
The suspect area has older homes with foundation drains known to be tied to laterals in some streets.
Isolating one street in the suspect area during rain removes most of its excess peak.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The flow meter in the suspect area reads three times high at all times
Wet weather inflow concentrated in the suspect subcatchment, largely from one street, is driving the excess
The suspect area uses three times more water indoors than its neighbours
Groundwater infiltration is equal everywhere and explains the peak

inference.explanation: Dry flows per home are equal, so indoor use and a constant meter error are ruled out. The excess appears only in rain and isolates to one street, fitting localised inflow.

nextClue.prompt: Which survey best pinpoints the connections on the isolated street?

options.label: A water billing comparison across subcatchments
House by house dye and smoke survey of foundation drains and roof leaders on that street
A meter recalibration for the suspect area

nextClue.explanation: A house level survey finds the actual connections that a disconnection program must remove.

clueText.nc-a: Billing matches dry flow, which is already known to be equal.
clueText.nc-b: The survey dye confirms foundation drain connections at eleven homes on the isolated street.
clueText.nc-c: Dry flows already match, so the meter is not reading three times high.

tasks.prompt: A sewer flows nearly full in dry weather, but CCTV shows the pipe is clean and correctly graded.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario dry weather capacity study. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Dry weather depth is 80 percent of diameter at average flow times.
CCTV shows a clean, well graded pipe with no deposits or roots.
Water billing for the catchment accounts for only half the metered sewer flow.
Night flow barely drops, and the extra flow is clear water entering at many joints on CCTV.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Chronic groundwater infiltration is consuming half the pipe capacity in dry weather
A partial blockage downstream is holding the depth up
The depth sensor is mounted wrong and over reads depth
Residents use twice the water shown on billing

inference.explanation: Clean graded pipe, billing at half the flow, minimal night drop, and clear water seen entering at many joints all fit infiltration. A downstream holdback would show on levels and CCTV, and billing contradicts double indoor use.

nextClue.prompt: Which calculation best quantifies the infiltration for the capacity report?

options.label: Night flow minus the estimated legitimate night water use, expressed per kilometre of sewer
Peak hour flow divided by pipe diameter
Billing total divided by number of homes

nextClue.explanation: Night flow less legitimate use isolates the groundwater share, and normalising by length allows comparison.

clueText.nc-a: The calculation gives a steady infiltration rate per kilometre that matches the joint entry seen on camera.
clueText.nc-b: Peak divided by diameter does not separate infiltration from real sewage flow.
clueText.nc-c: Billing per home describes water use, not the extra clear water in the sewer.

tasks.prompt: After sewer lining, wet weather peaks fall sharply but dry night flow stays exactly as high as before.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario before and after lining study. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Lining sealed the main sewer joints and the wet weather peak dropped by half.
Dry night flow after lining is unchanged from before lining.
Smoke testing after lining still finds roof leaders connected to laterals.
Lateral cameras show many private laterals with open joints below the water table.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The liner failed and the main joints still leak as before
The flow meter was changed during lining and reads differently
Rainfall increased after lining and masked the improvement
The remaining dry flow is entering through private laterals and connections that lining the main did not seal

inference.explanation: Peaks fell, so the liner worked on the main. Unchanged night flow with unsealed laterals below the water table and remaining roof connections locates the rest of the water outside the lined main.

nextClue.prompt: Which comparison best confirms laterals as the remaining source?

options.label: A rainfall comparison before and after lining
A liner thickness test on a sample
Paired night flow isolation, main plugged at the top of a reach, measuring lateral only inflow at night

nextClue.explanation: Plugging the main and measuring what laterals alone deliver at night isolates their contribution.

clueText.nc-a: Rainfall affects peaks, which already fell, not the steady dry night base.
clueText.nc-b: Liner samples do not measure lateral inflow below the water table.
clueText.nc-c: With the main plugged, lateral inflow alone accounts for nearly all of the unchanged night flow.

tasks.prompt: A basement floods with clear water in spring while the sanitary sewer in the street runs at normal depth.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario spring basement flooding case. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: The water entering the basement is clear and has no sewage odour.
Street sanitary manholes show normal depth during the flooding.
The home foundation drain discharges to a sump that runs almost constantly in spring.
When the sump pump is off for a test, water rises in the sump pit but no sewage appears.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: A sewer lateral blockage is forcing sewage into the basement
A watermain break under the street is flooding the basement
Groundwater at the foundation is overwhelming the sump, and the sanitary sewer is not the source
The sanitary sewer is surcharging into the basement

inference.explanation: Clear odourless water, normal street sewer depth, and a constantly running sump in spring fit groundwater at the foundation. A sanitary source would be odorous and match high street levels.

nextClue.prompt: Which check best confirms groundwater rather than a sewer source?

options.label: A watermain pressure log for one day
Sump pit watch with the pump off, logging rise rate, alongside street manhole depth at the same times
A lateral camera run in summer

nextClue.explanation: A timed rise in the pit with normal street depth separates foundation groundwater from sewer surcharge.

clueText.nc-a: One day of pressure does not explain a spring long, clear water pattern at the foundation.
clueText.nc-b: The pit rises steadily in spring while street depth stays normal, and the water stays clear throughout.
clueText.nc-c: A summer camera cannot reproduce spring groundwater conditions.

tasks.prompt: Dye testing a suspected cross connection shows dye from a storm drain appearing in the sanitary sewer.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario cross connection investigation. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Green dye poured into a parking lot catch basin appears in the sanitary manhole 10 minutes later.
No rain falls during the test and sanitary flow is otherwise at dry weather level.
The catch basin is mapped as storm on the drawings, but its outlet pipe runs toward the sanitary sewer.
A second catch basin on the same lot, dye tested the same day, goes correctly to the storm sewer.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The sanitary manhole was contaminated by dye from an earlier test
The one catch basin is cross connected to the sanitary sewer
All storm drainage on the lot goes to the sanitary sewer
Dye leaked through the soil from the storm pipe to the sanitary pipe

inference.explanation: One basin reaches sanitary in minutes in dry weather while its neighbour correctly reaches storm, which fits a single cross connection. Soil travel in 10 minutes and blanket lot wide connection are both contradicted by the paired test.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best documents the cross connection for correction?

options.label: Dye log with basin location, times, and photos of dye arriving at the sanitary manhole
A full lot drainage redesign drawing
A rainfall record for the test day

nextClue.explanation: A timed dye log with photos is the direct evidence a correction order relies on.

clueText.nc-a: The log shows dye in at 10:00 and dye at the sanitary manhole at 10:10, with the control basin going to storm.
clueText.nc-b: A redesign drawing plans the fix but does not prove which basin is crossed.
clueText.nc-c: No rain fell, so rainfall records add nothing to a dry weather dye result.

tasks.prompt: Inflow rises after a city program replaces old manhole covers, and the rise traces to one new development.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario new development inflow case. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: The development sewers are new, tight, and clean on CCTV.
Wet weather flow from the development is far above its dry weather flow per home.
Inspection finds the development storm pond outlet tied into the sanitary maintenance chamber during construction.
When the pond outlet is temporarily closed for a storm trial, the sanitary wet weather peak from the development falls sharply.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The storm pond outlet tied into the sanitary system is the inflow source
The new sewers leak groundwater at every joint
New homes use far more water in rain than in dry weather
The new manhole covers let rain pour into the sanitary sewer

inference.explanation: New tight sewers, a found pond tie in, and a closure trial that cuts the peak confirm the pond connection. New covers and joint leakage do not match a trial response at one outlet.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms the pond tie in before permanent correction?

options.label: CCTV report for the new sewers
Manhole cover specifications
Storm trial log with pond outlet open and closed, and sanitary flow from the development for both

nextClue.explanation: An open and closed trial with flows is a controlled test of the one suspected source.

clueText.nc-a: CCTV already showed the new sewers tight and clean.
clueText.nc-b: Cover specifications do not explain a peak that follows the pond outlet trial.
clueText.nc-c: The log shows the wet peak present with the outlet open and largely gone with it closed, in similar rain.

tasks.prompt: A flow meter shows a step jump in dry flow the day a new apartment building opens, then flow stays flat.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario flow step change at a new building. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Dry flow steps up by a steady amount the week the building is occupied and then stays flat.
Night flow also steps up by a smaller steady amount and stays flat.
The building has a groundwater drainage system for its underground parking that runs continuously.
No rain response changes in the catchment hydrograph after the building opens.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The building residents use water only at a constant rate all day and night
A sewer joint failed the week the building opened
The meter was damaged during building construction and now over reads
The building continuous parking drainage discharge explains the steady step in flow

inference.explanation: A flat step in both day and night flow with a known continuous drainage discharge fits a constant source. Resident use varies by hour, and a joint failure would track groundwater, not occupancy week.

nextClue.prompt: Which check best confirms the drainage discharge as the step source?

options.label: A CCTV run of the nearest sewer joint
Timed sampling and flow check at the building drainage outlet matched to the meter step size
A resident water use survey

nextClue.explanation: Measuring the outlet flow and matching it to the step size directly closes the balance.

clueText.nc-a: No joint defect pattern is stated, and the step follows occupancy, not groundwater.
clueText.nc-b: The outlet runs steadily at close to the step amount, day and night, matching the meter change.
clueText.nc-c: Resident use is not constant overnight, so a survey cannot explain a flat night step.

tasks.prompt: Two parallel flow meters on the same trunk disagree, one reading 20 percent higher at all flows.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario twin meter disagreement. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: The high meter reads about 20 percent above the other at low, medium, and high flows.
A timed bucket and stopwatch check at a test manhole matches the lower meter within a few percent.
The high meter sensor is found mounted with a 25 mm offset error in its depth setting.
Correcting the depth setting brings the two meters into agreement.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The lower meter is fouled and under reads at all flows
Infiltration between the two meters adds 20 percent
A depth setting offset in the high meter caused a constant proportional over reading
The trunk flow really is 20 percent higher at the high meter location

inference.explanation: An independent timed check matches the lower meter, a mounting offset is found, and fixing it restores agreement. Both meters are on the same trunk, so a real flow difference and a fouled lower meter are contradicted by the check.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best documents the meter fault for the data correction?

options.label: Calibration log with the timed check results, the offset found, and the after correction comparison
A rainfall log for the comparison period
An infiltration study of the trunk reach

nextClue.explanation: The calibration log ties the independent check, the fault found, and the restored agreement together.

clueText.nc-a: The log shows the timed check matching the low meter, a 25 mm offset, and agreement after correction.
clueText.nc-b: Rainfall does not explain a constant 20 percent gap at all flows in dry checks.
clueText.nc-c: The meters are on the same trunk with no reach between them to add infiltration.

tasks.prompt: Wet weather flow keeps rising year over year in a catchment where no new homes are built.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario ageing catchment trend. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Home count and water billing are flat over five years.
Wet weather peak flow rises steadily each year over the same five years.
CCTV over the period shows joint deposits and cracks increasing in the oldest clay sections.
A neighbouring catchment with newer plastic sewers shows a flat wet weather trend.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The flow meter drifts upward year over year
Progressive joint deterioration in the old clay sewers is admitting more wet weather water each year
Residents are using more water each year despite flat billing
Rainfall is increasing enough to explain the whole trend

inference.explanation: Flat billing rules out rising indoor use, worsening joint defects on camera track the rise, and the newer catchment under the same rain stays flat, which also rules out rainfall and points away from a single meter drift story.

nextClue.prompt: Which trend best confirms deterioration as the driver?

options.label: Annual rainfall totals alone
Annual billing totals alone
Year by year CCTV defect counts in the clay sections plotted with the wet weather peak trend

nextClue.explanation: Defect growth plotted with the flow rise links condition change to flow change over time.

clueText.nc-a: Rainfall is shared by both catchments, but only the clay one rises.
clueText.nc-b: Billing is already flat, so it cannot show a rising driver.
clueText.nc-c: Defect counts and wet peaks rise together in the clay catchment while the plastic catchment stays flat.

tasks.prompt: A sewer overflow occurs at a manhole in rain, but the sewer downstream is only half full at the time.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario overflow with capacity downstream. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: The overflow manhole surcharges and spills in a moderate storm.
The next two manholes downstream show flow at about half depth during the spill.
CCTV between them shows a short section where the pipe sags and holds water and debris.
Jetting the sag gives relief for weeks, then debris rebuilds and the spill returns.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: A sagging section is creating a local restriction that spills upstream while downstream runs half full
The downstream trunk is undersized for the whole catchment
The treatment plant is throttling flow back to this manhole
Inflow across the whole catchment exceeds total system capacity

inference.explanation: Half full downstream rules out a downstream capacity or plant throttle cause. A sag holding debris at one section, with relief after jetting and slow return, fits a local restriction.

nextClue.prompt: Which survey best confirms the sag as the restriction?

options.label: A plant influent flow log for the storm
Invert level survey through the reach showing the sag depth and length against design grade
A catchment wide flow study

nextClue.explanation: An invert survey quantifies the sag that the camera and the spill pattern point to.

clueText.nc-a: Plant flow does not locate a restriction between two manholes.
clueText.nc-b: The survey shows a 6 m sag holding 80 mm of water against an otherwise steady grade.
clueText.nc-c: A catchment study cannot explain downstream running half full during the spill.

tasks.prompt: A duplex lift station alarms on high level every night, and both pumps are found running with low discharge flow.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario duplex lift station, night alarms. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Both pumps run together at high level but the wet well level falls very slowly.
Discharge pressure is low and the force main flow meter reads well below normal.
Each pump tested alone against a closed test header produces normal pressure.
Opening the air release at the force main high point releases a large volume of air, after which flow returns to normal.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Both pump impellers wore out on the same night
Both check valves failed closed on the same night
The wet well floats are set wrong and call both pumps too late
Air bound force main is restricting both pumps, not a failure of the pumps themselves

inference.explanation: Pumps prove normal on a test header, yet together they cannot move flow until air is released at the high point, after which flow normalises. Simultaneous identical wear of both pumps is contradicted by the header test.

nextClue.prompt: Which log best confirms air binding for the station record?

options.label: Event log pairing low force main flow with the air release volume and the flow recovery after venting
Pump hour meter readings for the week
Float setting measurements

nextClue.explanation: Pairing low flow, vented air volume, and recovery documents the air binding event.

clueText.nc-a: The log shows flow at half normal, a long air release at the high point, and full flow within minutes after.
clueText.nc-b: Hour meters show running, not why flow was low while pumps ran.
clueText.nc-c: Float settings do not explain low flow with both pumps running.

tasks.prompt: One pump of a duplex pair trips its overload repeatedly while the other pump handles the station alone without trouble.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario duplex station, single pump trips. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Pump 2 trips on overload within minutes each time it starts, Pump 1 runs normally.
Pump 2 current draw is well above its nameplate while Pump 1 draw is normal.
Rotating Pump 2 by hand is stiff, and rags are found wound around its impeller when it is pulled.
After cleaning and reinstalling, Pump 2 current returns to normal and trips stop.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The overload relay for Pump 2 is faulty and trips at normal current
Pump 1 is stealing flow from Pump 2 through a shared header
Ragging of the Pump 2 impeller caused the high current and overload trips
The station inflow doubled and only Pump 2 cannot keep up

inference.explanation: Current above nameplate, stiff rotation, rags on the impeller, and recovery after cleaning all fit mechanical ragging of one pump. A faulty relay is contradicted by the genuinely high measured current.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms the ragging cause for the maintenance file?

options.label: Station inflow records for the week
Relay test certificate for Pump 1
Work log with Pump 2 current before and after cleaning and a photo of the rags removed

nextClue.explanation: Before and after current with the removed material photo is the direct proof of cause and cure.

clueText.nc-a: Inflow was handled by Pump 1 alone, so inflow did not double beyond one pump capacity.
clueText.nc-b: Pump 1 relay has no bearing on Pump 2 measured high current.
clueText.nc-c: The log shows Pump 2 at well above nameplate current before, and at normal current after rag removal.

tasks.prompt: A wet well level rises even while the duty pump runs, and falls only when the standby pump is also started.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario lift station capacity check. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Duty pump discharge pressure is normal but its flow by drawdown test is half its rated flow.
The pump impeller wear ring clearance measures well beyond the maker limit on inspection.
Motor current is slightly low, not high, and the pump runs smoothly with no rags found.
The standby pump drawdown test gives full rated flow.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The duty pump is air locked and moving no water at all
Internal wear in the duty pump is passing flow back inside the pump, cutting its output
The duty pump check valve is stuck fully closed
The wet well inflow has doubled permanently

inference.explanation: Normal pressure with half flow, low current, smooth running, no rags, and excessive wear ring clearance fit internal recirculation from wear. A closed check valve or air lock would give near zero flow, and the standby coping alone contradicts doubled inflow.

nextClue.prompt: Which test best confirms internal wear before the pump is rebuilt?

options.label: A force main pressure survey
Drawdown flow test paired with the wear ring clearance measurement in the pump inspection report
A float operation test

nextClue.explanation: Flow loss quantified by drawdown plus the measured clearance beyond limit confirms the wear mechanism.

clueText.nc-a: Force main pressure was normal, the loss is inside the pump.
clueText.nc-b: The report pairs half rated drawdown flow with clearance well beyond the maker limit.
clueText.nc-c: Floats start the pump correctly, the fault is output while running.

tasks.prompt: A lift station pump starts and stops every minute, but a staff gauge in the well shows the real level barely moving.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario lift station with bubbler level sensing. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: The panel level display swings up and down by 0.4 m within a minute while the staff gauge shows a steady level.
Pump starts and stops follow the swinging display exactly, not the steady real level.
The bubbler tube outlet is found partly blocked with grease and its purge pressure reads high.
After the tube is cleaned and purged, the display holds steady and pump cycles return to normal timing.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: A partly blocked bubbler tube is corrupting the level signal and driving the false rapid cycling
The start and stop floats are set too close together
Inflow is surging into the well every minute
The pump has lost capacity and must restart often to hold level

inference.explanation: The real level is steady on a staff gauge while the display swings and the pump follows the display, and cleaning the bubbler tube cures it. Float spacing cannot make a display swing against a steady gauge, and surging inflow would move the real level.

nextClue.prompt: Which log best confirms the sensing fault for the station file?

options.label: Float separation measurements
A pump capacity drawdown test
Paired level log, panel display against staff gauge readings, before and after the bubbler tube cleaning

nextClue.explanation: A paired display versus gauge log shows the signal error and its removal directly.

clueText.nc-a: Float spacing was not changed, yet cycling normalised when the tube was cleaned.
clueText.nc-b: Pump capacity does not explain a display that disagrees with a staff gauge.
clueText.nc-c: The log shows the display swinging against a steady gauge before cleaning, and both agreeing after.

tasks.prompt: A wet well refills rapidly right after the pump stops, even though night inflow is known to be low.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario lift station refill observation. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Level rebounds within a minute of pump stop by almost the full drawdown amount.
A listening check at the discharge hears flow running backward through the stopped pump line.
Inflow measured during a no pump period is slow and matches the low night rate.
Isolating the discharge gate valve stops the rebound completely.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Night inflow is much higher than believed
The stop float is set too high so the well looks refilled
The level sensor drifts upward after each pump stop
The check valve is leaking or stuck open and force main contents drain back into the well

inference.explanation: Rebound in a minute, backward flow heard, slow true inflow, and rebound stopping when the discharge is isolated all prove drainback through the check valve. A sensor or float fault would not produce audible backward flow.

nextClue.prompt: Which inspection best confirms the check valve fault before parts are ordered?

options.label: A level sensor calibration record
A night inflow measurement
Check valve internal inspection log noting the disc position and debris found holding it open

nextClue.explanation: Opening the valve and finding the disc held open is the direct confirmation.

clueText.nc-a: Sensor calibration cannot explain backward flow heard in the discharge pipe.
clueText.nc-b: True inflow was already measured slow during a no pump period.
clueText.nc-c: The log shows the disc wedged open by a piece of wood, matching the drainback volume each cycle.

tasks.prompt: Pumps at a station alternate correctly, but the wet well grease mat keeps reforming within days of cleaning.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario lift station with recurring grease mat. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: The mat reforms in days and is thickest near the inlet where flow enters quietly.
The station serves a food court whose interceptor service lapsed for six months.
A sister station with the same pumps and a serviced catchment has no mat problem.
Skimming the mat without any source work gives only a few clear days before it returns.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The wet well is too large and sewage goes septic making grease
Cleaning chemicals used on the mat are creating the new mat
Ongoing grease discharge from the unserviced food court catchment is reforming the mat
The pumps churn sewage into grease inside the wet well

inference.explanation: Rapid reformation, a lapsed interceptor upstream, and a clean sister station point to a continuing external grease load. Pumps cannot create grease, and skimming response shows removal without source control fails.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best links the mat to the catchment source?

options.label: Wet well dimension drawings
Interceptor service record for the food court paired with mat reformation dates at the station
Pump run hour comparison with the sister station

nextClue.explanation: Pairing lapsed service dates with reformation dates ties the mat to the uncontrolled discharge.

clueText.nc-a: Dimensions are the same as the sister station design, which stays clean.
clueText.nc-b: The record shows the mat returned within days throughout the six month service lapse.
clueText.nc-c: Run hours are similar at the clean sister station, so pumping does not explain the mat.

tasks.prompt: A station runs well by day but the high level alarm sounds on rainy days even though both pumps test at full capacity.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario lift station wet weather alarms. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Both pumps pass drawdown tests at full rated flow in dry weather.
Rainy day inflow by the flow trend is about double the combined pump capacity.
Upstream smoke testing finds storm connections in the station catchment.
In dry weather the station cycles normally with long rest periods.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The force main capacity halves in wet weather
Wet weather inflow above pump capacity, not a pump fault, causes the rainy day alarms
Both pumps lose capacity only when it rains
The floats are set too high and alarm before pumps can start

inference.explanation: Full capacity on test, inflow measured at double that capacity in rain, and storm connections found upstream explain alarms without any pump fault. Floats starting late would alarm in dry weather too.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms inflow as the limit for the upgrade study?

options.label: Rainy day inflow hydrograph plotted against combined pump capacity for the same storm
A dry weather drawdown test report
A float setting measurement

nextClue.explanation: Plotting measured inflow against known capacity in the same storm shows the exceedance directly.

clueText.nc-a: The hydrograph shows inflow above combined capacity for two hours while both pumps run continuously.
clueText.nc-b: Dry tests already proved full pump capacity, they cannot show the storm exceedance.
clueText.nc-c: Float settings do not change a measured inflow above total pump capacity.

tasks.prompt: After a pump is replaced, the station vibrates and flow is low, and the rotation arrow on the new motor does not match its wiring.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario station after pump replacement. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: The replacement pump vibrates, runs loud, and delivers about a third of expected flow.
Discharge pressure is low and the motor current is below normal.
The motor nameplate rotation arrow points opposite to the rotation observed at the coupling.
Swapping two leads to correct rotation restores full flow and quiet running.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The replacement motor was wired for reverse rotation, so the pump ran backward
The new pump is undersized for the station
The impeller was damaged in shipping and lost capacity
Air entered the wet well during replacement and locked the pump

inference.explanation: Reverse rotation observed against the arrow, low pressure and flow, and full recovery by swapping leads prove a wiring rotation fault. Shipping damage or undersizing would not be cured by lead swapping.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best documents the commissioning fault?

options.label: A pump sizing calculation
A shipping inspection report
Commissioning log with rotation check result, lead change, and flow before and after

nextClue.explanation: The commissioning log captures the rotation finding and the flow recovery in one record.

clueText.nc-a: Sizing was not changed, yet flow recovered fully, so size was not the fault.
clueText.nc-b: No shipping damage was found, and damage would not reverse with wiring.
clueText.nc-c: The log shows one third flow with reverse rotation and full rated flow after the lead swap.

tasks.prompt: A float switch fails to start the pump, and manual start works every time from the panel.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario lift station start failure. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: In hand mode the pump starts and runs normally every time it is tried.
In auto mode the pump never starts as the well fills to the alarm level.
The start float, lifted by hand in the well, does not change the panel input light.
A spare float connected at the panel terminals does change the input light correctly.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The pump motor has failed and cannot start in any mode
The panel power supply has failed completely
The stop float is stuck and holds the pump off
The installed start float or its cable has failed open, so auto control never sees the start signal

inference.explanation: Hand mode proves motor and power are good, the installed float gives no signal when lifted, and a spare float at the terminals works, isolating the fault to the installed float or cable. A stop float fault would not remove the start input light response.

nextClue.prompt: Which test best isolates float versus cable before replacement?

options.label: A panel power supply voltage log
Continuity and operation test of the removed float in a barrel of water, logged against a known good float
A motor insulation test

nextClue.explanation: Barrel testing the removed float against a good one separates a dead float from a cable break.

clueText.nc-a: Panel power is proven by hand mode running and the spare float input working.
clueText.nc-b: The barrel test shows the removed float never closes at any tilt while the spare closes cleanly.
clueText.nc-c: The motor already starts reliably in hand mode.

tasks.prompt: A station discharge pressure climbs month by month while pump flow falls, and the wet well levels are unchanged.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario station with rising discharge pressure. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Discharge pressure at the pumps has risen steadily over six months.
Force main flow has fallen over the same six months at the same wet well levels.
Both pumps test normally on the station test header.
A pigging trial run removes scale and flow and pressure return toward normal.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The wet well floats drifted and changed the pumping head
The pressure gauge has drifted high over six months
Force main internal scale buildup is narrowing the main and raising friction loss
Both pumps are wearing out together at the same rate

inference.explanation: Pumps test normal, levels are unchanged, and pigging restores flow and pressure, which locates the loss in the force main bore. A gauge drift would not change real flow or respond to pigging.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms the force main restriction?

options.label: Pressure and flow trend before and after pigging, with the scale material recovered logged
Pump test header results alone
Float level settings record

nextClue.explanation: A before and after trend with recovered material documents the restriction and its removal.

clueText.nc-a: The trend shows pressure falling and flow rising to near original values after pigging, with scale recovered.
clueText.nc-b: Header tests only prove the pumps, not where the system loss sits.
clueText.nc-c: Levels were unchanged, so float settings cannot explain the trend.

tasks.prompt: One duty cycle always ends in high level while the alternate cycle keeps up easily, with the same inflow pattern.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario alternating duplex station. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Pump A cycles hold level easily, Pump B cycles end in high level alarms.
Drawdown tests show Pump A at full flow and Pump B at half flow.
Pump B discharge gauge reads normal pressure while it runs.
Swapping the alternator so Pump B leads does not change which pump underperforms.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Pump B check valve is fully closed so it moves no water
Pump B itself has lost capacity, independent of control order or inflow
The alternator favours Pump A with longer run times
Inflow is higher whenever Pump B happens to be duty

inference.explanation: The fault follows the pump when control order swaps, drawdown quantifies Pump B at half flow, and normal pressure with half flow fits internal pump loss. A fully closed check valve would give near zero flow, not half.

nextClue.prompt: Which inspection best confirms the Pump B loss mechanism?

options.label: An alternator timing log
An inflow log by duty cycle
Pump B internal inspection with wear measurements, paired with its drawdown result

nextClue.explanation: Internal wear measurements paired with the measured flow loss confirm the mechanism.

clueText.nc-a: The alternator was already swapped and the fault stayed with Pump B.
clueText.nc-b: Inflow pattern was the same for both cycles by the station trend.
clueText.nc-c: Inspection shows Pump B wear clearances well beyond limits, matching its half flow drawdown.

tasks.prompt: A wet well foams and the pumps cavitate with noise and vibration at low level, though inflow is normal.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario wet well low level noise. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Noise and vibration start only when the level falls near the pump stop level.
A vortex is visible at the surface above the running pump intake at low level.
Raising the stop level for a trial ends the noise and vibration completely.
At higher levels the same pump runs quietly at full flow.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Vortexing at low level is drawing air into the pump intake and causing the cavitation like noise
The pump bearings are failing and noisy at all levels
The impeller is ragged and vibrates at all speeds
The force main is air bound and hammering the pump

inference.explanation: Symptoms tied to low level only, a visible vortex, and a stop level trial that cures them locate the cause at the intake surface. Bearing or rag faults would not switch off with level.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms the vortex cause for the setting change?

options.label: A rag inspection report
Trial log with stop level, noise observations, and flow at each level setting
A bearing vibration survey at high level

nextClue.explanation: A level by level trial log documents that submergence, not the pump internals, controls the noise.

clueText.nc-a: No rags are implicated by a fault that vanishes when level is raised.
clueText.nc-b: The log shows noise only below the trial stop level and quiet full flow above it.
clueText.nc-c: At high level the pump already runs quietly, so bearings are not the level linked cause.

tasks.prompt: At a duplex station the same pump has led every cycle for months, and the standby pump is stiff and slow when finally called.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario duplex lift station with an alternator fault. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Run hour meters show Pump A with nearly all the hours and Pump B with almost none over six months.
In hand mode Pump B starts and pumps normally through its own discharge.
In auto mode Pump B is never selected, though the alternator switch is set to alternate.
Panel inspection finds the alternator relay contacts welded in the Pump A position, and replacing the relay restores alternating duty.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The start float is faulty and can only call Pump A
The Pump B check valve is stuck shut so the panel locks Pump B out
A welded alternator relay kept Pump A as permanent lead and left Pump B idle until it stiffened from disuse
The Pump B motor has failed and the panel correctly avoids it

inference.explanation: Hours show one sided duty, Pump B runs and pumps normally in hand mode, it is simply never selected in auto, and a welded relay is found and cured by replacement. A failed motor or stuck check valve is contradicted by the normal hand mode run, and the float does call a pump, Pump A, every cycle.

nextClue.prompt: Which test best confirms the alternator fault for the panel record?

options.label: Auto mode cycle test log after relay replacement showing duty alternating between pumps each cycle
A Pump B motor insulation test
A start float operation test

nextClue.explanation: A cycle test showing selection alternating after the relay change confirms the control fault and its cure.

clueText.nc-a: The log shows Pump A and Pump B alternating lead duty across ten auto cycles after replacement.
clueText.nc-b: Pump B already runs normally in hand mode, so its motor is not the fault.
clueText.nc-c: The float calls a pump every cycle, the fault was which pump got selected.

tasks.prompt: A station overflows during a power outage that lasts longer than the wet well storage, though the generator starts.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario station outage overflow. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: The generator starts and carries the station lights and controls during the outage.
The generator is not sized or connected to run either sewage pump.
Wet well and upstream storage fill over three hours and the station overflows.
Utility power records confirm a three hour outage, and pump logs show no pumping in that window.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The floats failed when utility power was lost
The overflow was caused by storm inflow during the outage
The station has backup power for controls only, so no pumping is possible during a long outage
The pumps both failed mechanically during the outage

inference.explanation: Generator running controls only, no pump connection, no pumping logged, and storage filling over the outage duration explain the overflow without any pump or float failure. No storm is stated.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms the backup power gap for the upgrade case?

options.label: Pump repair invoices after the outage
Float test records after power returned
Generator load and connection schedule showing pumps not connected, paired with the outage timeline

nextClue.explanation: The connection schedule plus timeline proves the pumps could not run, which is the gap to fix.

clueText.nc-a: Pumps ran normally when utility power returned, so no repair was needed.
clueText.nc-b: Floats worked on generator powered controls throughout the outage.
clueText.nc-c: The schedule lists only lights and controls on the generator, and the timeline shows three hours with no pumping.

tasks.prompt: Station flow fell and discharge pressure rose in one step on the day of an emergency force main repair, and both stayed at the new values.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario force main after an emergency repair. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Flow and pressure changed in a single step on the repair date and stayed flat for months after.
Repair records show a 150 mm section installed in the 200 mm force main as a temporary fix.
Gauges either side of the repair section show most of the added pressure loss occurring across that short section at a set flow.
Both pumps test at full rated performance on the station test header.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Force main scale built up over months and raised the pressure
Both pumps wore out on the repair day
Air binding at the force main high point is adding the loss
The smaller repair section is a bottleneck adding friction loss at the repair point

inference.explanation: A step change on the repair date, a smaller section on record, pressure loss localised across that section by gauges, and full pump tests locate the loss at the repair. Scale grows gradually, not in one step, and air binding loss would sit at the high point, not across the repair section.

nextClue.prompt: Which survey best confirms the bottleneck for the permanent repair plan?

options.label: A pump wear inspection report
Pressure survey at a set flow with gauges either side of the repair section and at the high point
A six month pressure trend review

nextClue.explanation: Gauges at a set flow localise the loss to the section the permanent repair must replace.

clueText.nc-a: Pumps already test at full rating on the header.
clueText.nc-b: The survey shows the added loss across the 150 mm section and normal loss at the high point.
clueText.nc-c: The trend was a single step on the repair date, not a six month growth.

tasks.prompt: A pump runs but the wet well level does not fall, and the discharge pipe is cold while the pump motor is hot.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario station no discharge event. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: The duty pump runs, draws near normal current, and the well level stays unchanged.
No flow is heard in the discharge and the force main meter reads zero.
The pump discharge isolation valve is found fully closed after earlier maintenance.
Opening the valve restores normal drawdown immediately.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: A closed discharge isolation valve left after maintenance is blocking all pump output
The impeller has fallen off the pump shaft
The force main has burst outside the station
The check valve disc has detached and blocked the line

inference.explanation: A valve found fully closed after maintenance, with instant recovery on opening, is the direct cause. A burst main would show flow and a wet area, and a detached disc would not be cured by opening an isolation valve.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best prevents recurrence of this event?

options.label: Maintenance close out checklist with valve positions signed off, added to the station log
An impeller inspection report
A force main pressure test record

nextClue.explanation: A signed valve position checklist addresses the exact human step that caused the event.

clueText.nc-a: The checklist records every isolation valve position verified open before the crew leaves the station.
clueText.nc-b: The impeller was intact, the pump ran normally once the valve opened.
clueText.nc-c: The force main held pressure normally once flow was restored.

tasks.prompt: Station inflow by night is near zero, yet the pumps run many short cycles all night pumping the same water.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario station night recirculation. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Night inflow measured with pumps locked out for an hour is near zero.
With pumps in auto, the well draws down, stops, and refills to start level in minutes, all night.
Total pumped volume overnight is many times the measured inflow volume.
Holding the discharge gate closed for a trial night stops the cycling completely.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Residents discharge in pulses all night that the lockout test missed
The floats are set so close that a trickle causes constant cycling
Groundwater enters the well in pulses through its walls
Force main drainback through a leaking check valve is recirculating the same water all night

inference.explanation: Near zero locked out inflow, pumped volume many times inflow, and cycling stopping when the discharge is held closed prove recirculation through the check valve. Float spacing cannot create volume that is not entering the well.

nextClue.prompt: Which inspection best confirms the recirculation path?

options.label: A resident water use survey
A wet well wall inspection
Check valve inspection plus a timed rebound measurement after pump stop

nextClue.explanation: Finding the leaking valve and timing the rebound quantifies the drainback path.

clueText.nc-a: Locked out measurement already showed resident inflow near zero at night.
clueText.nc-b: Wall entry would continue with the discharge held closed, but cycling stopped.
clueText.nc-c: Rebound fills the drawdown in minutes and the valve disc is found scored and not seating.

tasks.prompt: A newly commissioned station floods its dry well pit with sewage whenever the lead pump runs at full speed.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario new station dry pit flooding. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Sewage appears in the dry pit only while the lead pump runs.
The leak sprays from a flanged joint on the lead pump discharge when it is pressurised.
The lag pump discharge flange does not leak at the same pressure.
Tightening and replacing the flange gasket on the lead discharge stops the leak completely.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The lag pump is backfeeding the lead pump discharge
Groundwater is entering the dry pit carrying sewage odour
A faulty flange gasket on the lead pump discharge is leaking under pressure
The wet well is overflowing into the dry pit through a wall crack

inference.explanation: Spray at one flange only under pressure, a sound lag flange at the same pressure, and a cure by gasket replacement locate a joint leak. A wall crack would leak with level, not only while one pump runs.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best closes the commissioning defect?

options.label: A groundwater sample from the pit
Pressure test log for the repaired flange at full pump pressure with no leak observed
A wet well level log

nextClue.explanation: A pressure test at working pressure with no leak is the acceptance evidence for the repair.

clueText.nc-a: The fluid was spraying sewage from a flange, not seeping groundwater.
clueText.nc-b: The log shows the flange dry through a full speed run after the gasket change.
clueText.nc-c: Wet well level was normal and the leak followed pump running, not level.

tasks.prompt: A force main loses pressure along its length and a wet area appears in a field midway, though the pumps are unchanged.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario force main leak investigation. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Station flow is normal but pressure at the discharge end has fallen over a week.
A wet area with sewage odour grows in a field above the force main route midway.
Isolating the downstream half of the main for a pressure hold test shows pressure falling in that half.
The upstream half holds pressure steady in the same test.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The end pressure gauge has failed low
A leak in the downstream half of the force main is losing flow and pressure
Both pumps have worn and cannot make pressure
Air at the high point is lowering end pressure

inference.explanation: Normal station flow, a growing wet odorous area over the route, and a hold test failing only in the downstream half locate a leak there. Pump wear would not fail a static hold test in one half only.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best locates the leak section for excavation?

options.label: Section by section pressure hold log narrowing the pressure loss to one valved section
Pump performance test results
End gauge calibration record

nextClue.explanation: Section hold results narrow the dig to the one section that cannot hold pressure.

clueText.nc-a: The log shows only the field section losing pressure, with tight sections on both sides.
clueText.nc-b: Pumps already deliver normal flow at the station.
clueText.nc-c: A gauge fault would not produce a wet odorous field or a failed hold test.
