tasks.prompt: Sewage from a long force main arrives at the discharge manhole black and strongly odorous, worst after weekends.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario long force main discharge quality. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Discharge is black with a strong rotten egg odour, worst on Monday mornings.
The force main holds about a full day of flow and the station pumps only a few times daily.
Weekend inflow is low, so sewage sits longest in the main before Monday pumping.
When pumping frequency is doubled for a trial week, discharge colour and odour improve markedly.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Long detention in the force main lets sewage turn septic before discharge
The wet well is the septic source and the main delivers it unchanged
Industrial discharge on Mondays blackens the sewage
The discharge manhole vent is blocked and traps odour there

inference.explanation: Worst after the longest holding period, a main holding a day of flow with few pump cycles, and improvement when detention is halved by trial all fit septicity in the main. A blocked vent would not blacken the sewage itself.

nextClue.prompt: Which log best confirms detention as the driver?

options.label: Industrial discharge records for Mondays
Manhole vent inspection notes
Pump cycle and detention time log plotted against discharge odour readings over the trial

nextClue.explanation: Detention time against odour across the trial directly tests the holding time effect.

clueText.nc-a: No industrial Monday pattern is stated, and odour tracks holding time, not the calendar alone.
clueText.nc-b: Vent notes do not explain black septic sewage arriving from the main.
clueText.nc-c: The log shows odour falling as calculated detention halves during the trial week.

tasks.prompt: A force main bursts twice in a year at the same low point fitting after pump starts.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario force main repeated bursts. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Both bursts occur at the same elbow at the low point of the main.
Pressure logging shows a sharp spike above working pressure in the seconds after each pump start.
Steady running pressure between starts is well within the pipe rating.
Slowing the pump start with a soft start trial removes the spike in the pressure log.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Steady working pressure is slowly weakening the fitting
The fitting material is corroding from hydrogen sulfide gas
Frost heave is crushing the fitting each winter
Start up pressure transients at the low point are bursting the fitting, not steady pressure

inference.explanation: Bursts at starts, spikes logged only at starts, normal steady pressure, and a soft start trial removing the spike prove a transient cause. Corrosion or frost would not follow pump starts or respond to soft starting.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms the transient cause for the fix?

options.label: A soil frost depth record
High speed pressure log at the low point during starts, before and after soft start fitting
A steady pressure average for the month

nextClue.explanation: Fast logging at the failure point during starts captures the spike that averages hide.

clueText.nc-a: Frost does not change with a soft start trial in the same season.
clueText.nc-b: The log shows spikes well above rating at starts before, and no spike after soft starting.
clueText.nc-c: Monthly averages hide second long spikes and were normal throughout.

tasks.prompt: Force main flow improves after pigging but falls again within weeks, and pigs return loaded with grit.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario force main grit returns. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Each pig returns carrying a large load of sand and grit.
Flow recovers after pigging, then declines again over a few weeks.
The wet well serving the main receives a gritty inflow and its grit removal upstream is poor.
A trial with improved upstream grit capture stretches the flow decline to many months.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Air is reaccumulating because the vent valves failed again
The pigs are undersized and never clean the main
Grit entering from the wet well catchment is redepositing in the force main between piggings
Scale is reforming in weeks from the sewage chemistry

inference.explanation: Grit loaded pigs, gritty inflow at the well, and a grit capture trial that stretches the interval identify the deposit as incoming grit. Scale chemistry or air would not load pigs with sand or respond to grit capture.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms the grit source for the upstream fix?

options.label: Pig return weights and grit content log plotted against upstream grit capture performance
Force main water chemistry analysis
Air valve inspection record

nextClue.explanation: Return weights against capture performance links what is in the main to what upstream lets through.

clueText.nc-a: The log shows heavy grit returns while capture is poor and light returns after capture improves.
clueText.nc-b: Chemistry explains scale, not pigs loaded with sand and grit.
clueText.nc-c: Vent valves affect air, not grit loads recovered by pigs.

tasks.prompt: A low point drain on a force main runs with gritty solids whenever it is opened, and pumps strain at start up.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario force main low point check. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Opening the low point drain discharges a long run of gritty solids before clear sewage follows.
Pump start current is high for the first minute, then settles to normal.
Flushing the low point section restores easy starts for several weeks.
The section upstream of the low point is a long flat run with low velocity at normal flow.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Air collects at the low point and blocks the starts
Solids settle in the flat low section and burden pump starts until flushed
The pumps are undersized for the force main length
The low point drain valve leaks solids from outside the pipe

inference.explanation: Gritty drain discharge, start strain that flushing cures for weeks, and a flat low velocity run fit settled solids. Air collects at high points, not low points, and undersized pumps would strain at all times, not just after settling periods.

nextClue.prompt: Which log best confirms settling in the low section?

options.label: A pump sizing review
A high point venting log
Low point drain discharge log with solids volume and the pump start current before and after flushing

nextClue.explanation: Solids volume at the drain paired with start current shows the burden and its removal.

clueText.nc-a: Sizing does not change with flushing, yet starts recovered.
clueText.nc-b: Venting a high point does not remove grit from a low point drain.
clueText.nc-c: The log shows pails of grit at the drain and start current normal for weeks after flushing.

tasks.prompt: Two stations share a force main, and when both run together flows fall and pressures rise at both stations.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario shared force main operation. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Each station alone delivers its full rated flow into the shared main.
When both run together, each delivers about two thirds of its flow and pressures rise at both.
Wet well levels and pump tests at both stations are normal.
Staggering run times by control change restores full flow delivery from both stations.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The shared main cannot carry both stations at full flow at once, so combined running throttles both
Both stations pumps fail whenever the other station runs
The shared main has a blockage that appears only on dual runs
The flow meters at both stations under read during dual runs

inference.explanation: Full flow alone, equal throttling together, normal pumps, and a cure by staggering fit shared main capacity. A fixed blockage would also cut single station flow, which is full.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms the shared capacity limit?

options.label: Meter calibration records for both stations
Dual run test log with flows and pressures for single and combined running at both stations
Individual pump test reports

nextClue.explanation: A controlled single versus combined test is the direct evidence of the shared limit.

clueText.nc-a: Meters at two stations would not both shift only during dual runs and recover with staggering.
clueText.nc-b: The log shows full flows singly and matched two thirds flows with high pressure together.
clueText.nc-c: Pump tests were already normal at both stations.

tasks.prompt: A manhole frame sits 40 mm below the road surface in a dip, and the sewer below surcharges only at that manhole in rain.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario manhole in a road dip. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Road water ponds over the low frame in moderate rain.
The cover is an open hole type and the frame seal is broken.
Sewer flow upstream and downstream of the manhole is normal during the surcharge.
Raising and sealing a trial frame on the same structure ends the local surcharge in similar rain.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The sewer at the manhole is undersized and surcharges there first
Groundwater pressure lifts the manhole base in rain
A partial blockage sits exactly under this manhole
Surface water enters through the low unsealed frame and cover in the dip

inference.explanation: Ponding over a low open cover, normal flow on both sides, and a cure by raising and sealing the frame prove surface entry. An undersize or blockage would disturb flow beyond the one manhole.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best documents the frame entry for the repair list?

options.label: Storm photo and level log at the frame showing ponding depth and the surcharge response to sealing
CCTV of the sewer through the manhole
Groundwater levels near the manhole

nextClue.explanation: Photos and levels at the frame during rain document the entry point a frame repair fixes.

clueText.nc-a: The record shows ponding over the holes as the manhole surcharges, and no surcharge after sealing in similar rain.
clueText.nc-b: The sewer through the manhole already shows normal flow on both sides.
clueText.nc-c: Groundwater does not respond to sealing a road surface frame.

tasks.prompt: Manhole walls show heavy white and yellow deposits and the concrete is soft and crumbling above the flow line.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario manhole wall deterioration. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Damage is worst above the flow line and the benching below water is sound.
A rotten egg odour is strong at the manhole and gas readings show hydrogen sulfide present.
The manhole receives a long force main discharge that arrives septic.
A newer plastic manhole downstream on the same discharge shows no wall damage.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The concrete was poorly mixed when the manhole was built
Roots are crushing the manhole walls
Hydrogen sulfide from septic discharge is corroding the concrete above the flow line
Road salt is corroding the manhole from the surface down

inference.explanation: Damage above the flow line only, sulfide gas present, septic force main discharge arriving, and a plastic structure unaffected fit sulfide corrosion of concrete. Salt damage would start at the top and poor mix would affect the whole structure including benching.

nextClue.prompt: Which check best confirms sulfide attack for the lining decision?

options.label: A road salt application record
A root defect log for the manhole
Wall pH and depth of soft concrete profile above the flow line, logged with gas readings

nextClue.explanation: Low wall pH with soft depth above the flow line, alongside sulfide gas, is the signature of sulfide attack.

clueText.nc-a: Salt records do not explain damage that spares the top and benching but attacks the middle wall.
clueText.nc-b: No roots were reported in the manhole structure.
clueText.nc-c: The profile shows strongly acidic soft concrete above the flow line and sound hard benching below it.

tasks.prompt: A manhole channel is worn into a deep groove offset from the outlet, and flow splashes and leaves debris on the benching.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario manhole benching inspection. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: The formed channel no longer lines up with the outlet pipe after an upstream pipe was relined thicker.
Flow hits the benching edge, splashes, and drops rags and grit on the bench.
Debris builds on the benching and washes in slugs to the outlet during high flow.
Reforming the channel to line up with the outlet for a trial section ends the debris buildup.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The manhole is too deep and flow falls too far
A misaligned benching channel is dropping debris that later washes out in slugs
Upstream homes discharge debris in slugs at high flow
The outlet pipe is too small and backs debris onto the bench

inference.explanation: Channel offset after relining, splashing at the bench edge, buildup on the bench, and a cure by reforming the trial channel prove the benching geometry fault. An undersized outlet would pond flow, not splash it onto the bench.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms the channel fault?

options.label: Outlet pipe sizing calculations
Manhole inspection photos showing the offset channel, splash marks, and bench debris pattern
Upstream discharge records

nextClue.explanation: Photos of offset, splash, and debris pattern document the geometry fault directly.

clueText.nc-a: Sizing does not explain a channel that visibly misses the outlet.
clueText.nc-b: Photos show flow striking the bench edge at the offset and debris stranded exactly in the splash zone.
clueText.nc-c: Upstream discharges do not explain debris stranded on one bench in a splash pattern.

tasks.prompt: Steps inside a manhole are heavily corroded and one step pulls free by hand during inspection.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario manhole step safety inspection. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Several steps show deep corrosion and scale, worst in the zone above the flow.
One step pulls out of the wall with hand pressure alone.
Hydrogen sulfide odour is noted at the manhole on every visit.
A nearby newer manhole with plastic steps shows no step damage.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Sulfide corrosion has weakened the metal steps to a safety failure, so entry must not rely on them
The steps were installed loosely and were never sound
The steps are designed to pull free as a safety feature
Road vibration alone corroded the steps

inference.explanation: Deep corrosion in the sulfide zone, a step failing by hand, repeated sulfide odour, and sound plastic steps nearby fit corrosion weakening. Loose installation would not show deep metal corrosion across several steps.

nextClue.prompt: Which action record best addresses the step hazard?

options.label: Entry log recording the failed step, a no climb decision using a ladder or tripod system, and a step replacement order
A note to climb carefully on the remaining steps
A road vibration complaint to the city

nextClue.explanation: Recording the failure, changing the entry method, and ordering replacement addresses the hazard directly.

clueText.nc-a: The log bars step use at this manhole, sets ladder entry, and orders corrosion resistant steps.
clueText.nc-b: Climbing carefully still relies on corroded steps that failed by hand pressure.
clueText.nc-c: Vibration does not produce the sulfide zone corrosion pattern seen on the steps.

tasks.prompt: A manhole lid rattles under traffic and rain entering the joint is seen as a clean water stream in dry follow up checks after storms.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario manhole lid and frame joint. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: The lid rocks in the frame and traffic noise is reported by residents.
After storms, a clean water stream enters at the frame joint for hours, then stops.
In dry weather with no recent rain, no water enters at the frame joint.
The sewer joints near the manhole are tight on CCTV with no infiltration seen.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Pipe joint infiltration near the manhole is the entry
A watermain leak feeds the frame joint stream
Condensation inside the manhole forms the stream
Rain and shallow groundwater enter through the loose frame joint after storms

inference.explanation: Entry at the frame joint only after storms, none in dry weather, and tight pipe joints on camera locate the path at the frame. A watermain leak would run in dry weather too, and condensation does not form a stream.

nextClue.prompt: Which trial best confirms the frame joint path?

options.label: A CCTV run of the nearby sewer joints
A watermain pressure log
Flood test with dyed water ponded around the frame, watching for dye at the joint inside

nextClue.explanation: Dyed water ponded at the frame appearing inside is a direct path test.

clueText.nc-a: Pipe joints were already shown tight on camera.
clueText.nc-b: A pressure log cannot show which opening the water uses.
clueText.nc-c: Dye appears at the frame joint inside within minutes while pipe joints stay clear.

tasks.prompt: Roots fill a manhole from one incoming pipe joint, while the outgoing sewer beyond is clear.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario manhole root mass. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: A root mass hangs from the incoming pipe joint inside the manhole.
CCTV beyond the manhole shows the outgoing sewer clear and free of roots.
CCTV up the incoming pipe shows roots only in its last 2 m near the manhole.
A large tree stands beside the manhole, its roots lifting the frame slightly.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Roots grow from the outgoing sewer back into the manhole
The root mass was washed down and caught at the manhole
Roots enter at the incoming joint right at the manhole, beside the tree
Roots fill the whole incoming sewer from far upstream

inference.explanation: Roots only in the last 2 m of the incoming pipe, a clear outgoing sewer, and a tree lifting the frame locate entry at the manhole joint. A mass washed down would not be attached growing from the joint with clear pipe beyond.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best locates the root entry for the repair?

options.label: A tree removal assessment
Manhole and short CCTV log showing root attachment at the incoming joint and clear pipe both ways beyond 2 m
A full catchment CCTV survey

nextClue.explanation: A focused log proves entry at one joint, which a joint repair can seal without wider work.

clueText.nc-a: Tree assessment does not show the joint gap the roots are using.
clueText.nc-b: The log shows roots attached at the joint gap and clear pipe upstream beyond 2 m and downstream throughout.
clueText.nc-c: A catchment survey is wider than the located defect requires.

tasks.prompt: During surcharge a manhole cover lifts and shifts, and sewage spills around the frame though the cover was in place before the storm.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario surcharge cover displacement. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: The cover is found shifted half off the frame after the storm peak.
Witness timing places the spill at the peak of the sewer surcharge.
The frame shows fresh scrape marks matching the cover edge moving.
Other manholes on the same surcharged reach with bolted covers stayed sealed and did not spill.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Flood water from the road washed the cover off from above
Surcharge pressure lifted the unsecured cover and spilled at the peak
A vehicle struck the cover and knocked it off before the storm
The cover was left off by a crew after inspection

inference.explanation: Spill at the surcharge peak, fresh scrape marks from movement, and bolted covers on the same reach staying sealed fit pressure lifting from below. No vehicle strike or crew visit is stated, and road water flows over, not under, a cover.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best supports fitting a bolted or sealed cover at this manhole?

options.label: Surcharge level log for the reach with the spill timing and the bolted cover comparison
A vehicle damage report
A crew work schedule for the storm day

nextClue.explanation: Levels with spill timing plus the sealed comparison make the case for a secured cover.

clueText.nc-a: The log shows spill only at peak surcharge and no spill at bolted covers on the same reach and storm.
clueText.nc-b: No vehicle damage was reported and scrape marks match lifting, not impact.
clueText.nc-c: No crew visit was scheduled at this manhole on the storm day.

tasks.prompt: Odour complaints cluster at one drop manhole where a sewer falls 3 m, and complaints peak in the morning.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario drop manhole odour cluster. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Sewage drops 3 m inside the manhole and splashes into the outlet channel.
Gas readings at the manhole show hydrogen sulfide present, highest after the morning flow peak.
Manholes upstream and downstream without drops draw few complaints.
Sealing the drop manhole cover vents for a trial week sharply reduces complaints at street level.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Turbulence at the drop strips hydrogen sulfide from the sewage and vents it at that manhole
A dead animal in the manhole causes the odour cluster
The morning sewage itself is stronger across the whole town
A nearby restaurant grease bin causes the complaints

inference.explanation: Complaints at the one drop structure, sulfide readings peaking after flow peaks, quiet non drop neighbours, and a sealing trial cutting complaints fit gas stripping at the drop. A town wide strength change would affect other manholes too.

nextClue.prompt: Which log best confirms the drop as the release point?

options.label: Restaurant bin cleaning records
Town wide sewage strength results
Complaint times plotted against manhole gas readings and flow peaks at the drop structure

nextClue.explanation: Matching complaints to gas and flow at the one structure confirms the release point.

clueText.nc-a: Bin records do not explain sulfide readings inside the manhole.
clueText.nc-b: Town strength does not explain why only the drop manhole draws complaints.
clueText.nc-c: The plot shows complaints following sulfide peaks at the drop manhole within the hour, day after day.

tasks.prompt: A subdivision at the end of a long flat sewer complains of rotten egg odour from home drains in summer.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario subdivision odour in summer. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: The sewer run to the subdivision is long, flat, and flows slow and deep in summer.
Sewage sampled at the subdivision end is dark with sulfide present, while sewage at the run start is fresh.
Complaints are worst in hot weather and after low use nights.
A flushing trial of the long run reduces odour complaints for the following week.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Home drain traps in the subdivision are all faulty
A landfill near the subdivision causes the drain odours
The treatment plant odour drifts back through the sewers
Sewage goes septic in the long slow run and releases sulfide at the subdivision end

The grit entered the reach between the jetting and the bucketing

inference.explanation: Cloudy water but a remaining grit bed after jetting, loads of compacted grit by bucket, a bare invert after, and complaints ending fit a method mismatch for heavy compacted material. The bucket removes deposits, not pipe wall, as the bare intact invert shows.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best sets the future method for this reach?

options.label: Before and after CCTV pair with material volumes recorded for jetting and for bucketing
Jetting truck hour records
Complaint counts alone

nextClue.explanation: Paired camera results with volumes compare what each method actually removed.

clueText.nc-a: The pair shows a grit bed left by jetting and a bare invert after bucketing, with loads logged.
clueText.nc-b: Hours measure effort, not the grit bed left behind in the pipe.
clueText.nc-c: Complaints ending supports the result but does not show which method removed the bed.

tasks.prompt: A jetting crew reports a reach clean, but a camera run the same day shows a continuous silt bed along the invert.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario cleaning verification failure. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: The crew report says clean, based on the jetting water running clear at the downstream manhole.
Same day CCTV shows a silt bed covering the invert for most of the reach.
The jet nozzle used was a general flushing nozzle, and no material was collected at the manhole.
A second pass with a penetrating nozzle and collection removes pails of silt and the camera then shows a bare invert.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The camera run disturbed the invert and created the silt bed
Silt entered the reach in the hours between jetting and the camera run
The silt bed is the pipe invert itself misread on camera
Clear running water was a false sign of clean, the first jetting moved silt along without removing it

inference.explanation: A same day camera showing a continuous bed, no collection at the manhole, and a second pass removing pails of silt prove the first pass left the material. Silt does not enter a whole reach in hours or get created by a camera.

nextClue.prompt: Which verification best closes this cleaning job?

options.label: The crew clear water note alone
A downstream water clarity sample
Post cleaning CCTV with the bare invert shown, attached to the work order with material volumes removed

nextClue.explanation: Camera verification with volumes is the objective close out for a cleaning claim.

clueText.nc-a: Clear water was already shown to be a false sign on this reach.
clueText.nc-b: A clarity sample repeats the same false sign that failed the first time.
clueText.nc-c: The close out shows a bare invert on camera and pails of silt recorded for the second pass.

tasks.prompt: Flow in a cleaned sewer improves, but odour at the downstream manhole gets worse for two days after cleaning.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario post cleaning odour effect. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Cleaning removed a thick layer of old septic solids from the reach invert.
For two days after, downstream odour readings are higher than before cleaning.
Disturbed solids are seen arriving at the downstream manhole in slugs after cleaning.
By the third day, with the reach running clean, odour falls below the old level.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The cleaning damaged the pipe and sewage is leaking to the surface
A new odour source started upstream on the cleaning day by chance
Cleaning disturbed septic solids that released a short burst of odour downstream before conditions improved
Cleaning chemicals added to the sewer caused the two day odour

inference.explanation: Removed septic solids, slugs arriving downstream, a two day rise, then odour below the old level once the reach runs clean fit a disturbance effect. No chemicals or damage are stated, and a chance new source would not fade as the reach clears.

nextClue.prompt: Which log best explains the pattern to the complainants?

options.label: A pipe damage inspection report
Odour readings before, during the two days after, and after day three, aligned with the cleaning record
A chemical delivery record for the cleaning truck

nextClue.explanation: A dated odour trend aligned with cleaning shows a short disturbance, then improvement.

clueText.nc-a: No damage was found, and flow improved with a clean invert on camera.
clueText.nc-b: Readings peak for two days as slugs arrive, then fall below the pre cleaning level and stay there.
clueText.nc-c: No cleaning chemicals were used beyond water jetting on this job.

tasks.prompt: Night flow analysis shows a catchment minimum of 18 L/s, while billed night water use estimates only 6 L/s of sewage.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional Ontario night flow analysis. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Minimum sewer flow at 3 a.m. is steady at 18 L/s on dry nights.
Estimated legitimate night sewage from water use is about 6 L/s.
The gap of about 12 L/s is steady all night and varies with season, higher in spring.
CCTV in the catchment shows widespread joint defects below the water table.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: A single large leak adds a steady 12 L/s all year
About 12 L/s of the night flow is groundwater infiltration entering through the defective joints
Residents discharge 18 L/s of sewage at 3 a.m. every night
The flow meter over reads by a steady 12 L/s

inference.explanation: A steady gap three times legitimate use, seasonal variation with groundwater, and widespread defects below the water table fit distributed infiltration. A single leak would not vary seasonally, and a meter offset would not match the defect pattern or season.

nextClue.prompt: Which calculation best reports the infiltration share?

options.label: Night minimum minus legitimate night use, reported as infiltration and as a share of average daily flow
Peak day flow minus night minimum
Billed use divided by home count

nextClue.explanation: Subtracting legitimate use from the night minimum isolates infiltration and its share of flow.

clueText.nc-a: The report states about 12 L/s infiltration, varying seasonally, against 6 L/s legitimate night flow.
clueText.nc-b: Peak minus minimum mixes daytime sewage with the infiltration signal.
clueText.nc-c: Billing per home does not separate groundwater from sewage at night.
